newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Italy bans Swiss beef imports.
newsitem.headline: Italy bans Swiss beef imports.

text.p: Italy on Thursday banned beef imports from Switzerland, which is second only to Britain in the number of cattle infected with "mad cow" disease, a spokesman at the veterinary office of the Swiss Economics ministry said.
The Italian measure also forbids the import of beef from stocks not proven to be free of the disease, know as Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE).
BSE is a brain-wasting disease that scientists say may be linked to a human equivalent, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease.

Switzerland has reported 223 BSE cases from 1990 up to this September despite a measure introduced in December, 1990, which forbids feeding cattle beef bone and remains that could help spread the disease.
Italy previously imposed some restrictions on Swiss beef imports, but had lifted them in September. Other countries have imposed bans on Swiss beef imports.
Last month the Swiss cabinet proposed the slaughter of up to 230,000 cattle in a bid to eradicate mad cow disease in Switzerland and to restore consumer confidence.
